players.product: gas turbines & grid technology for data-center power

quarterly_data.signal: Siemens Energy (press-call host, opening statement): order intake and revenue increased, with revenue of EUR 17.9 billion in Q3 FY2026; profit before special items tripled year on year to a 14.2% margin; the wind business (Siemens Gamesa) achieved a positive result for the first time in 15 quarters; Siemens Gamesa will use the name Omterra as Siemens Energy moves to a standalone brand.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue EUR 17.9 billion; margin before special items 14.2%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Christian Bruch: if he remembers correctly, data centers were roughly 20% of gas turbine orders by capacity in the quarter, a little less than the previous quarter as Siemens Energy consciously strikes a balance, and a lower share for transformers; he calls it an important market that is here to stay but not as dominating as some reporting suggests. The Middle East (especially Saudi Arabia, UAE, Oman and Qatar) accounted for roughly 30% of the quarter's gigawatts in a rough estimate, with several gigawatts of large projects.
quarterly_data.figure: data centers ~20% of gas turbine orders (capacity); Middle East ~30% of gigawatts

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Christian Bruch: the order backlog stands at EUR 162 billion of orders and excludes slot reservations, which Siemens Energy deliberately keeps limited; reservation agreements, structured like a down payment that lapses if the turbine is not bought, are discussed at around 10%-20%.

CEO Christian Bruch: Siemens Energy is confident of reaching the upper end of its profit margin guidance range and kept the range unchanged because of quarterly seasonality; the EUR 8 billion free cash flow guidance remains robust despite significant capex in Q4; it is optimistic for 2027 and will give 2027 and medium-term guidance in November (annual press conference on 11 November).
quarterly_data.figure: free cash flow guidance EUR 8 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Christian Bruch: over the first three quarters the wind business posted a small double-digit loss; the offshore order book covers 2027 and 2028 and new offshore orders are needed for 2029; cash break-even in wind is expected in 2028; the SG 7.0 onshore turbine, successor to the 5.X, is launching with smaller sales numbers so far.

CEO Christian Bruch: Siemens Energy closed the acquisition of Camlin (digital grids) this quarter to broaden Grid Technologies, and earlier acquired CIC in England, a producer of ceramic cores, to secure supply for its Gas Services business; a possible carve-out of Transformation of Industry is under internal discussion with no timeline or decision yet.
